section_summary: This section consists chiefly of 1947 correspondence with American holders of Japanese government, municipal, and electric utility bonds. The State Department records holdings but says it cannot predict repayment or peace treaty terms; it directs holders toward bondholder councils and, where applicable, claims against vested Japanese assets. Related letters address sterling bonds, securities trading, and German and Hungarian obligations.

people.role: Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs

people.name: A. W. Overby

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Campbell inquiry
subfiles.about: Refers Archibald Campbell's question about redeeming Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards Campbell's letter and its acknowledgment for State Department reply.

subfiles.title: Campbell inquiry about Imperial Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Asks whether American-held Imperial Japanese gold bonds might be redeemed.
subfiles.summary: Campbell cites good-faith purchases and reports of valuables found in Japan.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to Campbell
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Campbell's inquiry and refers it to State.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says State handles foreign bond inquiries.

subfiles.title: State reply to Campbell
subfiles.about: Explains policy toward defaulted Imperial Japanese dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: State cannot predict settlement terms, suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council, and offers to record bond and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: State reply to Terhune
subfiles.about: Responds to Terhune's Tokyo Electric Light bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: The 1943 Treasury filing was not a claim; State outlines private bond enforcement, possible council assistance, and information it will record.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Terhune inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Terhune's letter and Treasury's reply.
subfiles.summary: Treasury refers the Tokyo Electric Light bond question to State.

subfiles.title: Terhune inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about reimbursement or investor protection for his Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: Terhune describes a $1,000 bond reported to Treasury in 1943.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply to Terhune
subfiles.about: Refers Terhune's bond inquiry to State.
subfiles.summary: The poor OCR indicates a Treasury acknowledgment and referral for reply.

subfiles.title: State reply to Hatten
subfiles.about: Requests identifying facts about purported Kiewan Electric bonds.
subfiles.summary: State finds no record of a U.S. issue and asks for issuer, dates, rate, and currency.

subfiles.title: Justice referral of Hatten inquiry
subfiles.about: Refers Hatten's Kiewan Electric inquiry for direct reply.
subfiles.summary: Justice encloses Hatten's letter and its response.

subfiles.title: Hatten request for claim forms
subfiles.about: Requests forms to claim payment on overdue Kiewan Electric bonds and coupons.
subfiles.summary: Hatten reports hearing that bondholders might receive payment.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply to Hatten
subfiles.about: Explains why the office cannot accept a Kiewan Electric claim.
subfiles.summary: No property of the issuer has been vested; Justice refers the broader question to State.

subfiles.title: State reply to Scherzinger
subfiles.about: Answers an inquiry about a Nippon Electric Power dollar bond.
subfiles.summary: State explains its bondholder policy, suggests the protective council, and requests bond and citizenship details for its files.

subfiles.title: Scherzinger inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests information about unpaid interest on a Nippon Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Scherzinger says coupons were paid before the war and asks when arrears might be addressed.

subfiles.title: State reply to Weinstein
subfiles.about: Accepts information on Weinstein's Tokyo Electric Light bond for State files.
subfiles.summary: State records the holding, explains that repayment remains uncertain, and refers Weinstein to the protective council.

subfiles.title: Weinstein bondholding report
subfiles.about: Reports a $1,000 Tokyo Electric Light bond and citizenship details.
subfiles.summary: Weinstein asks State to record bond number 46314, last paid in June 1941.

subfiles.title: State reply to Aoki
subfiles.about: Explains treatment of Japanese dollar, sterling, and franc bonds and possible claims against vested assets.
subfiles.summary: State distinguishes private and government obligations, identifies American, British, and French bondholder councils, and lists information holders should submit. It cannot predict peace treaty terms or Office of Alien Property decisions and says Congress will determine blocked property's disposition.

subfiles.title: Aoki inquiry for Japanese American committee
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Asks whether seized funds could pay defaulted Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The committee seeks the status of dollar, sterling, and franc bonds.

subfiles.title: Elliott bondholding report
subfiles.about: Requests recording of three Oriental Development Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: Elliott describes three $500 government-guaranteed debentures due in 1953.

subfiles.title: State reply to Elliott
subfiles.about: Records Elliott's Oriental Development Company holdings.
subfiles.summary: State explains its bondholder policy, suggests contacting the protective council, and asks for citizenship details.

subfiles.title: State reply to Itatani
subfiles.about: Advises on claims for Tokyo Electric Light coupons.
subfiles.summary: State points to possible Office of Alien Property claims before June 1, 1947.

subfiles.title: Itatani coupon inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks how to collect December 1941 Tokyo Electric coupons.
subfiles.summary: Itatani requests payment information and any necessary forms.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Alexandria consulate
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Alexandria
subfiles.about: Provides replies concerning Molossi's City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: The instruction distinguishes British council handling of sterling bonds from American council handling of dollar bonds.

subfiles.title: Specimen reply to dollar bondholders
subfiles.to: American holders of City of Tokyo dollar bonds
subfiles.about: Sets out a model response for dollar bondholders.
subfiles.summary: The model explains State policy, council representation, uncertainty over settlement, and bondholding information to submit.

subfiles.title: Specimen reply to sterling bondholders
subfiles.to: American holders of City of Tokyo sterling bonds
subfiles.about: Sets out a model response for sterling bondholders.
subfiles.summary: The model recommends the British Council of Foreign Bondholders and offers to record holdings.

subfiles.title: Alexandria consular despatch
subfiles.about: Forwards Molossi's inquiry about American holders of Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: The consul requests guidance; the referenced Molossi letter is not reproduced in this section.

subfiles.title: State reply to Baumgartner
subfiles.about: Answers a question about Imperial Japanese sinking fund gold bonds.
subfiles.summary: State cannot predict repayment, suggests the protective council, and invites additional holding and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Baumgartner inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Baumgartner's bond inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Treasury refers the question and its reply to State.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply to Baumgartner
subfiles.about: Refers Baumgartner's bond question to State.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says State will consider and answer the inquiry.

subfiles.title: Baumgartner inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about liability on her Imperial Japanese sinking fund bond.
subfiles.summary: Baumgartner had reported the bond on a 1943 Treasury census form.

subfiles.title: State reply to Watson
subfiles.about: Addresses Watson's Japanese, German, and Hungarian obligations.
subfiles.summary: State distinguishes private from government bonds, offers to record holdings, and cannot forecast settlement or vesting action. It suggests contacting the protective council and Office of Alien Property.

subfiles.title: Watson securities inventory
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese, German, and Hungarian bonds and asks about vesting and payment.
subfiles.summary: Watson identifies issuers, values, coupons, and claims already filed for two Japanese issues.

subfiles.title: State reply to McMillan
subfiles.about: Explains where to inquire about trading in estate-held Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: State says exchange trading was suspended in December 1941 and refers Stevenson to the SEC.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of McMillan correspondence
subfiles.about: Forwards a congressional inquiry about Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: Treasury encloses McMillan's correspondence and its reply.

subfiles.title: Stevenson estate inquiry
subfiles.about: Seeks guidance on disposing of two Japanese bonds in an estate.
subfiles.summary: Stevenson asks which agency can explain wartime trading restrictions.

subfiles.title: Treasury reply to McMillan
subfiles.about: Explains Treasury's view of dealings in Japanese securities.
subfiles.summary: Treasury reports no direct prohibition where only the issuer is Japanese, notes voluntary dealer restraint, and refers the matter to State.

subfiles.title: State reply to Whitcomb
subfiles.about: Responds to missing Tokyo Electric Light interest payments.
subfiles.summary: State suggests a claim for coupons through 1941 against possibly vested funds.

subfiles.title: Reference slip for Whitcomb letter
subfiles.about: Routes Whitcomb's March 1 letter.
subfiles.summary: A departmental reference slip identifies the attached bondholder letter.

subfiles.title: Whitcomb interest inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about unpaid interest on her Tokyo Electric Light bond.
subfiles.summary: Whitcomb says June 1940 was the last coupon she could cash.

subfiles.title: Interim State reply to Shutack
subfiles.about: Sends claims guidance pending a detailed reply.
subfiles.summary: State encloses its May 8 press release on claims against vested Japanese assets.

subfiles.title: Justice referral of Shutack inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Shutack's bond question for reply.
subfiles.summary: Justice encloses her letter and its response.

subfiles.title: Shutack claim-form inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks whether she should claim on a Shinyetsu Electric Power bond.
subfiles.summary: Shutack requests forms before the June 1 deadline.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply to Shutack
subfiles.about: Explains that no Shinyetsu Electric property has been vested.
subfiles.summary: Justice cannot entertain the claim and refers the broader inquiry to State.

subfiles.title: State reply to Dreux
subfiles.about: Explains prospects for German and Japanese government bondholders.
subfiles.summary: State cannot predict peace settlements or payment, recommends the protective council, and lists bondholder information it will record. It also describes the June 1 deadline for claims against vested assets.

subfiles.title: Dreux inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks whether German and Japanese government bonds might be paid.
subfiles.summary: Dreux requests information on foreseeable payment plans.

subfiles.title: State reply to John Steneck & Sons
subfiles.about: Addresses a client's City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: State explains equal treatment with British holders, suggests asking the British bondholder council about redemption limitations, and notes possible vested-asset claims.

subfiles.title: Steneck inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks how to claim on a client's City of Tokyo sterling bonds.
subfiles.summary: Steneck describes roughly £580 in bonds reportedly due in 1920 and 1921.

subfiles.title: Paull inquiry about Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Requests a reply concerning Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: The handwritten, poorly recognized letter appears to follow up a September 1947 communication.

subfiles.title: State reply to Ecuer
subfiles.about: Records Ecuer's Tokyo Electric Light bond holdings.
subfiles.summary: State explains its policy, suggests the protective council, and notes the June 1 deadline for claims against vested assets.

subfiles.title: Ecuer bondholding report
subfiles.about: Reports two Tokyo Electric Light bonds and naturalization details.
subfiles.summary: Ecuer supplies bond numbers, approximate purchase information, and the last interest date.

subfiles.title: Denby bondholding supplement
subfiles.about: Supplies details on Taiwan Electric and Imperial Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Denby lists purchases, bond numbers, coupon status, and citizenship by birth.

subfiles.title: Campbell bondholding supplement
subfiles.about: Supplies details of his Imperial Japanese dollar bond.
subfiles.summary: Campbell gives rate, dates, value, purchase price, last interest, and citizenship.

subfiles.title: State acknowledgment to Campbell
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Campbell's supplemental bond information.
subfiles.summary: State will file the details for possible future consideration.

subfiles.title: Hess inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks about Nippon Electric Power operations, repayment, and claims.
subfiles.summary: Hess seeks guidance on the bonds' value and possible reparations treatment.

subfiles.title: Interim State reply to Hess
subfiles.about: Provides interim claims information.
subfiles.summary: State sends its May 8 press release while preparing a fuller answer.

subfiles.title: Justice referral of Smedley inquiry
subfiles.about: Forwards Smedley's comments on redeeming Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Justice encloses Smedley's letter and its reply for State consideration.

subfiles.title: Office of Alien Property reply to Smedley
subfiles.about: Explains claims against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: Justice identifies vested City of Yokohama property, supplies claim materials, and refers policy questions to State.

subfiles.title: Smedley Japanese bond inquiry
subfiles.about: Asks whether seized funds or government action will repay Japanese bondholders.
subfiles.summary: Smedley cites the City of Yokohama loan and urges stronger U.S. action to secure payment.

subfiles.title: State reply to Smedley
subfiles.about: Explains State policy on Japanese municipal bonds.
subfiles.summary: State cannot promise repayment or treaty provisions, suggests the protective council, and offers to record Smedley's holdings and citizenship.

subfiles.title: State reply to Moseley
subfiles.about: Answers questions about Taiwan Electric Power bond value and unpaid coupons.
subfiles.summary: State cannot value the bonds or predict repayment. It suggests consulting the U.S. Attorney about claims against vested assets, contacting the protective council, and supplying citizenship details for State's records.
